newsitem.title: USA: New York Times, Guild reach tentative labor contract.
newsitem.headline: New York Times, Guild reach tentative labor contract.

text.p: The New York Times said Friday it reached a tentative agreement with The Newspaper Guild of New York on a labor contract extension through 2003 that includes a 2 percent annual salary increase beginning in 1997.
The agreement was reached after extensive negotiations with the Guild, which represents 1,500 clerical, business, news and editorial employees of the newspaper, the Times said.
The contract is subject to ratification by the Guild's members at the Times, and a ratification meeting is planned for September, the newspaper said.

The contract includes a one-time, 3 percent bonus for 1996 and a ban on all layoffs for the entire term of the extended agreement for regular full-time and part-time employees currently on the Times' payroll, it said.
Times Publisher Arthur Sulzberger Jr. said the newspaper was delighted to have reached the agreement.
"Now we can turn all of our attention to the exciting launch next month of The Times's new six-section, color daily newspaper for the next generation of readers and advertisers," he said.
Guild President Barry Lipton said the contract was "a superior agreement" that addresses the concerns of the Guild's members.
The Guild represents 3,700 workers at more than 20 media organizations in the metropolitan area.
